components.name: Glass and Sphere
components.description: The signature object: a deep blue sphere with a pink rim behind vertical fluted-glass ribs.
components.css: .ds-glass{position:relative;overflow:hidden;isolation:isolate;width:360px;height:300px;background:linear-gradient(180deg,#eef8fd 0%,#dbf2fc 38%,#a9d6f2 72%,#5f9fdc 100%)}.ds-orb{position:absolute;z-index:0;border-radius:50%;aspect-ratio:1;width:92%;left:18%;top:6%;background:radial-gradient(circle at 64% 38%,#8cc4f2 0%,#3d84d6 22%,#164f9c 46%,#072D59 74%,#041a36 100%);box-shadow:inset 34px 0 60px -14px rgba(253,110,136,.95),inset 8px 0 18px rgba(255,190,205,.55),-30px 0 90px -20px rgba(253,110,136,.55);animation:ds-drift 16s cubic-bezier(.45,0,.55,1) infinite alternate}.ds-ribs{position:absolute;z-index:1;inset:0 40% 0 0;-webkit-backdrop-filter:blur(14px) saturate(150%);backdrop-filter:blur(14px) saturate(150%);background:repeating-linear-gradient(90deg,rgba(255,255,255,.42) 0,rgba(255,255,255,.06) 9px,rgba(7,45,89,.10) 22px,rgba(253,110,136,.16) 30px,rgba(255,255,255,.38) 34px);-webkit-mask-image:linear-gradient(90deg,transparent,#000 28%,#000 100%);mask-image:linear-gradient(90deg,transparent,#000 28%,#000 100%)}@keyframes ds-drift{from{translate:0 0}to{translate:-4% 3%}}@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ds-orb{animation:none}}

narrative.overview:
A calm, icy world of cold daylight. The ground is a pale seal blue that deepens toward a saturated sky at the bottom of the hero; ink is a deep navy; one crimson pink marks the single thing to do. The idea goes in on the left as light, large type and a pill-shaped field, and on the right a deep blue sphere with a pink rim sits behind vertical fluted-glass ribs that refract it and shift with the pointer. That glass-and-sphere is the one signature object, and it recurs as the same object at reduced scale behind the top of every app page.

Density is generous on the persuasion surface (128px section rhythm, 60 to 96px light headlines) and moderate in the app (860 to 960px column, cards with 24 to 32px padding). Everything interactive is a pill; everything that contains is a softly rounded rectangle on a white surface with a hairline border and a navy-tinted ambient shadow. Light and dark mode follow the device: in dark, the ground becomes a near-black navy, surfaces become navy, and the pink stays the same pink.

The world refuses the SaaS split hero with a product screenshot and a row of fake customer logos. Proof is limited to the real tools the product sends to, set as plain type.
keyCharacteristics: Seal-blue ground, navy ink, a single crimson pink accent.
Hanken Grotesk at weight 300 for display, with an italic second line on its own line.
One glass-and-sphere object per viewport, never scattered blur.
Soft navy-tinted ambient shadows; a pink glow only under the primary button.
Device decides light or dark; no toggle.

rules.name: The One Pink Rule
rules.body: Crimson pink marks the one primary action on a screen plus state (selection, focus, checked, progress). Secondary actions use seal blue or an outline pill. Two pink buttons on one screen is a bug.

rules.name: The Navy-On-Pink Rule
rules.body: Text and icons on crimson pink are navy (`navy`). White on pink fails contrast and is not part of this world.

rules.name: The Device Decides Rule
rules.body: Light and dark come from `prefers-color-scheme` only. Every color token has a dark counterpart; the pink is the one value that does not change.

rules.name: The Italic Second Line Rule
rules.body: Display and headline text is light 300 with the second phrase in italic 300, set on its own line ("Rough idea in. *Buildable spec out.*"). The italic never goes bold.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Headings and labels are sentence case. There is no uppercase tracked label style in this system.

rules.name: The One Object Rule
rules.body: The glass-and-sphere appears once per viewport as one specific object: the hero, the closing band, or the sky band on app pages. It hides below 1180px on app pages and below 980px in the closing band. Never break it into scattered blurred shapes.

rules.name: The Earned Blur Rule
rules.body: Backdrop blur belongs to the glass ribs, the sticky top bar, and a card floating over the glass. It is not a general card treatment.

dos: Do give each screen exactly one crimson pink action and set its label in navy.
Do set display and headline text in Hanken Grotesk 300 with the italic phrase on its own line.
Do make every control a pill (999px) and every container a 14 to 28px rounded rectangle on `surface` with a 1px hairline.
Do show the glass-and-sphere as one object per viewport, and hide it rather than squeeze it at narrow widths.
Do derive every color from the token pair so dark mode follows the device.
Do draw icons as stroked SVG (1.7 to 1.8px stroke, round caps) in `currentColor`.
donts: Don't build a split hero with a product screenshot or a row of customer logos; name only the real tools the product sends to, as plain type.
Don't put white text on crimson pink or use pink as a large background fill.
Don't scatter blurred shapes or apply backdrop blur to ordinary cards.
Don't add uppercase tracked labels above headings.
Don't use `faint-slate` for running text or notes people need to read; it is for placeholders and axis labels.
Don't use emoji or text characters as icons.
